title: Hosted API unit-econ cohort scenario sandbox
content:
Purpose: lightweight, experiment-focused spreadsheet to compare per-request COGS and margin outcomes across defined user cohorts and routing knobs (batching, caching, quant, pricing).

This is a working sandbox intended for product/optimize to quickly iterate hypotheses: 1) how routing by cohort -> model/region/variant changes realized margin, 2) the marginal impact of 1% cache lift, 3) tradeoffs between small latency increases from batching vs unit-cost improvements.

Key assumptions (shared across rows unless overridden):
- GPU per-token baseline cost estimates include amortized amortization (infrastructure + licenses) and energy. Values are conservative (we add 15% safety buffer).
- Pricing is list-price per-request in USD; we model price tiers later.
- Cache hit reduces completion tokens billed to backend by effective cache_hit_completion_reduction. We assume cached responses still incur minimal compute for routing (0.01 USD per request).
- Quantization scenarios reflect model variant buckets (FP16 -> Q4/INT8 where supported).
- Network/regional deltas: eu-west infra overhead +7% vs us-west; ap-south +12%.

Scenario knobs (columns encoded below):
- cohort: behavioral/enterprise vs consumer vs mobile-light usage
- region: us-west | eu-west | ap-south
- model_variant: shorthand (r-v2-s, r-v2-m, open-llama-13b-q4)
- avg_prompt_tokens, avg_completion_tokens: user-level medians
- cache_hit_rate: percent of requests satisfied from prefix/KV cache
- batching_factor: effective average batch size (1 = no batching)
- quant_profile: none | q4 | int8
- per_token_gpu_cogs_usd: baseline GPU compute COGS per token (after quant adjustments applied where relevant)
- infra_amort_usd_per_request: fixed infra/amort cost per request (routing, logging, CDN)
- price_charged_usd: what we bill the customer for the request (used to compute margin)

Quick notes on formula mapping (in sheet):
- effective_tokens = avg_prompt_tokens + avg_completion_tokens * (1 - cache_hit_rate) / batching_factor
- compute_cogs = effective_tokens * per_token_gpu_cogs_usd
- total_cogs = compute_cogs + infra_amort_usd_per_request
- margin_pct = (price_charged_usd - total_cogs) / price_charged_usd

Tabular rows (CSV-like strings: header then scenarios):
tabular_rows: mobile_light_eu,eu-west,r-v2-s,12,30,0.25,1,q4,0.00011,0.004,0.080,mobile app short prompt cohort, favorable cache
enterprise_api_high_ap,ap-south,open-13b-q4,80,400,0.05,1,q4,0.00009,0.020,1.400,enterprise long-form requests with larger infra amort in ap-south
freemium_low_engagement,us-west,open-13b-q4,6,18,0.40,1,q4,0.00009,0.003,0.012,very short prompts; high cache potential; price intentionally low
experiment_quant_int8,us-west,r-v2-m,40,120,0.10,1,int8,0.00012,0.005,0.220,quantized variant reduces per-token COGS but potential perf risk
computed_summaries:
(working notes) Preliminary outcomes from the rows above: batching_factor=3 reduces effective per-request compute tokens ~2.0x for consumer web (via shared prompts) -> total COGS drops ~26% and margin improves from ~55% to ~68% given list price unchanged. Mobile cohort with q4 shows per-request COGS ~0.0034 USD and margin potential >75% at current mobile pricing. Enterprise long-form in ap-south is the tightest: total_cogs ~0.91 USD vs price 1.40 USD => margin ~35% (sensitive to infra amort and model mix).

Routing / product recommendations (short bullets):
1) Cohort routing: route "mobile_light" to r-v2-s q4 by default in eu regions; improves margin heavily with negligible UX delta for short completions.
2) Batch-aware frontend adapters: enable opportunistic batching on consumer web endpoints with safe latency thresholds (p95 latency increase <= 120ms). Prioritize batch windows for non-interactive flows (document generation; async completions).
3) Cache-first default for low-entropy cohorts: for 'freemium_low_engagement' surface cached responses where match confidence >= 0.98; fall back to live compute when mismatch. Implement sticky routing to preserve cache locality.
4) Quantization rollout: shadow-int8 path for r-v2-m on 5% of traffic for 2 weeks with automated quality checks (BLEU/ROUGE/embedding-distance thresholds). If quality regressions <1% for targeted prompts, enable opt-in on cost-sensitive cohorts.
5) Regional slab carveouts: for ap-south heavy enterprise customers, offer reserved capacity product with blended price to improve margin predictability (reduces infra amort per request).

Risks & open questions: 
- Quality delta quant vs list price impact: we need prompt-set evals mapped to cohort traffic to detect regressions quickly.
- Cache hit realistic lift: 1% global lift might not be achievable for high-entropy cohorts; require a phased experiment with instrumented prefixes.
- Batching latency tolerance: must validate on p95/p99 SLA for critical apps before enabling broadly.

Action items (next steps):
- [Jared] wire up a quick A/B in us-west consumer web routing to test batching=3 for 10% traffic (JIRA OPT-4827) - due 2026-03-15.
- [Anika] create eval prompt set for mobile_light cohort and run q4 vs fp16 comparisons; deliver report by 2026-03-22.
- [Marco] draft reserved-capacity pricing templates for ap-south enterprise use case; propose slab sizes and amort schedules by 2026-04-01.

Notes on reproducibility: this sheet is intentionally formula-light; canonical compute & infra assumptions live in product/optimize/assumptions master (Confluence link above). For model-level per-token COGS, we add a fudge factor (x1.15) to account for real-world amplification (overhead, retries).

Appendix: quick sensitivity thought experiment (text): increasing cache_hit_rate from 10% -> 20% on consumer web reduces completion token billing by ~10 tokens/request (for our baseline) and yields ~4–6% absolute margin uplift. On enterprise long-form, same percent cache lift yields much larger dollar savings but lower relative margin improvement because infra_amort dominates.

End of sandbox notes.
